title: Authored learning module
description: Envelope around one LearningModuleDefinition. The `module` property is byte-for-byte the shape declared in apps/web/src/module/moduleFormat.ts, so a consumer does JSON.parse(file).module and casts. Everything else in the envelope is authoring evidence — reading-rate arithmetic, deliberate exclusions, the window re-cut against Mission-Slate §4.7 — and no runtime reads it.

card.description: One screen. `throughSeconds` is where this card's presentation target ENDS, measured from module start; the format cannot express a minimum dwell, so no author can turn a target into a lock-out. The last card's value is the whole module length and must be 180.

excerpt.description: A quoted primary source. Verbatim always; runtime never generates or paraphrases one.

conceptIds.description: Empty on a frame card, which teaches none and says so rather than being absent from a list.

codexCardIds.description: Propositions this card is the sole source for. This is the field that makes the duel's answerable-from-the-module claim checkable rather than asserted.

presenter.description: The embodied System presenter: an imported rigged GLB shown in a transparent hologram layer. Missing/loading renders no presenter and emits a dev QA error — never a primitive stand-in.

scene.description: A card's cinematic slideshow: an ordered set of narration/subtitle beats over a set of provenanced visuals. Optional and decorative — a card with no scene renders as flat instruction.

beat.description: One narration/subtitle beat. `text` is spoken by the voiceover provider and shown verbatim as the subtitle.

audio.description: A future external-audio cue. No URL or key is authored now; only the shape a later provider will fill.

visual.description: One floating document/image panel with full provenance. `src` is a local imported asset path, never a runtime hotlink. A PROJECT_RECONSTRUCTION may not caption itself 'actual'.

video.description: A generated cutscene clip that plays inside a case file alongside its document (the video half of the media split). SOURCE-TOLERANT: `src`/`poster` are OPTIONAL — a clip is authored with its full provenance BEFORE the MP4 exists, and the player renders no <video> (the document and its question still show) rather than a broken frame. When present, `src`/`poster` are local imported asset paths (leading `/`), never a runtime hotlink. A generated clip is a PROJECT_RECONSTRUCTION and may not caption itself 'actual'. Mirrors ModuleVideo in apps/web/src/module/moduleFormat.ts.

check.description: A short pre-authored mastery check placed after a concept card. Truth is carried per option by its stable `correct` flag, not by position, so the answer need not be first. Two authored shapes: a FIXED-LIST check (`options`) — single-select marks one correct, multiple-select two or three and the learner picks the exact set; or a POOLED check (`correctOption` + `distractorPool`, single-select only) that draws a different subset of distractors and a fresh order each mission attempt, so three playthroughs never present the same option set. The learner cannot advance past the concept until they answer correctly. Pays no XP and is not timed.

selection.description: Single- or multiple-select. Optional; an absent value is 'single', so content authored before this field keeps its meaning. A pooled check is always single-select.

drawCount.description: Pooled checks only: how many options a sitting shows (the answer plus drawn distractors). Default 4.

correctOption.description: Pooled checks only: the one defensible answer, always shown. Must be marked correct.

distractorPool.description: Pooled checks only: the misconception-encoded wrong options. Every entry must be `correct: false`, and the pool must be at least `drawCount` deep so three attempts never repeat an option set.
